{{Short description|Code represented by sparse graph}}
A '''sparse graph code''' is a [[code]] which is represented by a [[sparse graph]].

Any [[linear code]] can be represented as a graph, where there are two sets of nodes - a set representing the transmitted [[bit]]s and another set representing the constraints that the transmitted bits have to satisfy. The state of the art classical [[error-correcting code]]s are based on sparse graphs, achieving close to the [[Shannon limit]]. The archetypal sparse-graph codes are [[Robert G. Gallager|Gallager's]] [[low-density parity-check code]]s.
